Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Apex Asset Management Fourth Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, the instructions for joining the question and answer session will be given at that time. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Jamie Chen, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Jamie Chen: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Asset Management's fourth quarter results. Joining me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Financial Officer; and Michael Torres, Chief Investment Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Jamie, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the fourth quarter. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by exceptional client loyalty, record assets under management, and disciplined execution across our strategies, setting a strong foundation for the year ahead.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, Alex. From a financial perspective, Apex Asset Management delivered strong results in the fourth quarter. Our revenue was $1.82 billion, representing a 12% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by higher average AUM, resilient fee rates, and robust net inflows across channels. Our expenses were $1.23 billion, resulting in net income of $450 million. We continue to manage our expenses prudently while investing in key growth initiatives.

Before moving on, let me highlight two critical areas: our client metrics and operating margin trends, which truly demonstrate the scalability and durability of our business model. First, on client retention and new client acquisition, which I view as the lifeblood of our operations. In a quarter marked by market swings, persistent inflation around the 2.5-3% range, Fed rate adjustments to between 5.25-5.50%, and geopolitical tensions, we posted a trailing 12-month dollar-weighted retention rate of 96.2% as of December 31st, up 120 basis points from 95% a year ago. This outperforms industry norms and reflects deep client trust.

By segment, institutional clients—62% of our $1.45 trillion AUM—achieved 97.8% retention, with pensions and sovereign wealth funds favoring our multi-asset credit approaches that beat benchmarks by 180 basis points net of fees. Intermediary and RIA channels hit 95.1%, supported by seamless model portfolio integrations with partners like Schwab and Fidelity. High-net-worth individuals and family offices reached 94.7%, lifted by bespoke alternatives allocations.

Geographically, the Americas, at 68% of AUM, led with 97% retention, bolstered by U.S. defined contribution plans under IRA auto-enrollment trends. EMEA managed 95.5%, holding firm against MiFID II costs via UCITS ESG equity funds that retained €4.2 billion from European defined benefit schemes. APAC, 14% of AUM, improved to 93.2% from 91% year-over-year, countering China headwinds with customized private markets for Singapore and Australian superannuation funds.

This strength stems from our Apex Client360 platform, now reaching 78% of clients with AI-powered real-time analytics, machine learning-based predictive risk models from two decades of data, and TCFD-aligned ESG scoring—boosting Net Promoter Scores by 15 points to 82. Our 1,200 client advisors increased touchpoints 22% quarter-over-quarter using Salesforce and Bloomberg integrations. Plus, our core-plus fixed income and thematic equities generated 2.1% alpha over the MSCI World Index, surpassing peers per Morningstar.

Shifting to new client acquisition, we captured $28.4 billion in net new assets, up 22% from last year and ahead of guidance, bringing year-to-date to $52.1 billion or 4.6% of opening AUM—top-quartile per Coalition Greenwich. Organic flows drove 89%, with minor tuck-ins like our Latin American RIA stake.

Wins were product-led: $14.2 billion into alternatives, highlighted by the Apex Private Credit Fund at 11.2% annualized yields rivaling Blackstone, and $6.8 billion in semi-liquid infrastructure for yield-hungry insurers. Intermediaries added $9.1 billion, 35% from RIAs adopting our white-labeled SMAs. By asset class: equities 42%, fixed income 28%, multi-asset 18%, alternatives 12%.

Regionally, Americas led with $19.7 billion (69%), including a $2.5 billion U.S. pension mandate and wirehouse expansions. EMEA added $5.2 billion via SFDR approvals, edging Amundi. APAC surged 45% year-over-year to $3.5 billion through Hong Kong partnerships and yen-hedged plays on BOJ shifts.

Forward, we're prioritizing Apex NextGen for mass affluent clients in the $15 trillion U.S. wealth transfer, targeting 10% share with Addepar integrations onboarding 15,000 retail accounts quarterly. Institutionally, climate risk analytics in pitches align with PRI demands. We see Q1 retention over 96% and $25-30 billion NNA, supporting 5-7% organic growth even in a 5-10% market pullback.

Now, turning to trends in our operating margin, which highlight our efficiency. We define it as adjusted operating income over net revenues, stripping non-recurring items like amortization. Q4 came in at 32.5%, expanding 230 basis points year-over-year from 30.2% and 110 basis points sequentially from Q3's 31.4%. Trailing twelve months: 31.8% versus 29.1% last year—strong versus peers like T. Rowe Price's mid-teens or Franklin Templeton's 25-27%.

Revenue growth of 12% to $1.82 billion reflected 14% higher average AUM from equity/alternatives rallies (S&P up 18% YTD) and $28 billion organic inflows. Horizon ETFs, like our iShares-inspired core suite, drew $15 billion. Fees held at 42 bps despite compression, aided by alternatives at 22% of AUM (up from 18%) fetching 85-120 bps.

Expenses rose just 7% to $1.23 billion, yielding 500 bps leverage. Comp/benefits, 48% of revenue, grew 9% on performance pay but fell to 42% of revenue via better professional utilization; targeting sub-40% long-term like Vanguard. G&A flat at $320 million or 18%, with EuroPacific synergies cutting rates 2%. Tech spend of $150 million YTD on AWS cloud and AI optimization trimmed middle/back-office costs 15% per AUM; robo-advisory at $50 billion scales at sub-10 bps marginal cost.

By region, Americas margins hit 35% on $20 billion 401(k)/RIA flows amid Fed cuts. EMEA reached 30%, up 300 bps on €12 billion UCITS ESG ETFs under SFDR. APAC at 25% improves via Japan/India pivots to $10 billion alternatives.

Our 'Scale Through Diversification' drives this: ETFs to 35% AUM, alternatives 22%, digital platforms at 50%+ margins. ESG across 40% portfolios adds 10-15 bps premiums. Q1 margins eyed at 33.5-34.5%, full-year 32.5%, toward 35% by 2026 on 8-10% AUM growth and tech leverage, despite volatility or talent risks.

Thank you. I'll now hand over to Michael.

Michael Torres: Thank you, Lisa. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in equities, which comprise 45% of AUM at $650 billion, riding U.S. large-cap tech rallies including the Magnificent Seven amid AI buildouts—our active funds like Apex Global Growth beat MSCI World by 450 bps at 22% annualized. ETFs grew to 28% or $405 billion, with the Apex S&P 500 ETF netting $12 billion institutional inflows. Fixed income at $480 billion saw $10 billion NNM, conservatively positioned at 4.2-year duration for Fed's 75 bps 2024 cuts, with short-duration/floaters at 5.2% yields drawing DC plans. Alternatives at $225 billion led by private credit at LIBOR +550 bps (10-12% net) and infrastructure, pulling $8 billion from pensions.

We are navigating the current market environment by leveraging our AI-driven Apex Insight engine covering 95% of portfolios for 50 bps beta enhancement via dynamic factors, partnering with NVIDIA for 90% faster VaR modeling, and launching new products like buffer ETFs, ESG target-dates, and interval funds.

Alex Rivera: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. This includes accelerating AUM growth through diversified channels targeting 12-15% expansion and $120-150 billion net inflows; deepening tech differentiation with $200 million in AI/ML for 20% efficiency gains and cost/revenue under 55%; and regional expansion to lift non-U.S. AUM to 35% via Europe acquisitions, APAC SWF partnerships, and EM debt, growing alternatives to 22% with 12% yields. Backed by $450 million investments at 8% of revenue and $2.5 billion liquidity for 18-20% ROE.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Morningstar.

Sarah Jenkins: Thanks, and good morning, team. I wanted to dive into your outlook for AUM growth. With markets volatile and fee pressures ongoing, can you walk us through management's expectations for organic flows, market beta capture, and any inorganic opportunities? Specifics on asset class and regional drivers would be great.

Alex Rivera: Good morning, Sarah. Happy to provide a detailed update on our AUM outlook. We closed the quarter with record AUM of $1.45 trillion, up 18% year-over-year and 5% quarter-over-quarter. This blends 10% market appreciation from equity beta and fixed income duration with $28 billion net new money in Q4.

Recapping drivers: Equities at $650 billion (45%) gained from U.S. tech rallies, especially Magnificent Seven AI plays; Apex Global Growth Fund returned 22% annualized, topping MSCI World by 450 bps. ETFs hit $405 billion (28%) on $12 billion inflows to low-cost cores like Apex S&P 500. Fixed income $480 billion (33%) added $10 billion NNM with 4.2-year duration for Fed cuts, floaters at 5.2% yields post-SVB shifts. Alternatives $225 billion (16%) drew $8 billion to private credit at LIBOR +550 bps (10-12% net) and infrastructure from pensions.

By region: North America 60% of Q4 NNM ($17 billion) via Merrill/Morgan Stanley; EMEA 25% ($7 billion) on UCITS ETFs and MiFID II; APAC 35% YoY growth ($4 billion) in Singapore ESG tapping $3 trillion SWF shifts.

For FY25, we guide 12-15% AUM growth to $1.65-$1.70 trillion: 7-9% market (equities mid-teens on 12% S&P earnings, fixed 4-6% to 3.75% Treasury, alts 8-10% IRRs), $120-140 billion organic (4-5%, $30-35 billion quarterly: 55% retail/RIA via Apex Wealth's 2.5 million users/$250k average with robo tax efficiency; $60 billion institutional from OCIO/target-date like $5 billion Taft-Hartley infrastructure), 1-2% inorganic tuck-ins.

Organic focus: 98% fee retention at 42 bps (65 bps active, 15 bps ETFs). Initiatives: Q1 ETFs (buffer with 80-100% upside/20% protection, SFDR Article 9 ESG, RIA interval seeded $2 billion); Apex Insight AI for 50 bps tilts; NVIDIA risk tech; APAC 25% NNM CAGR via Shanghai JV/Tokyo J-REITs; EMEA AIFMD illiquids; LatAm double via Brazil reforms. Inorganic: $50 billion RIA boutiques at sub-40 bps.

Risks: geopolitics/15% drawdown (18-month liquidity), fee compression (mitigated by 55 bps privates), SEC rules. Tailwinds: $5 trillion retirement/ETF/demo alts by 2030 per Cerulli. We're set for top-quartile growth.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you. And a follow-up on trends in your strategic initiatives for client acquisition?

Lisa Patel: Thanks, Sarah. Our client acquisition ties directly into priorities like Apex NextGen robo-hybrid for mass affluent, converting 18% pipeline, and institutional ESG/climate pitches. This supports $120-150 billion inflows while maintaining margins.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Kim with Goldman Sachs.

David Kim: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of the Apex Global Growth Fund?

Michael Torres: Good morning, David. Absolutely. The Apex Global Growth Fund has been a standout, managing $25 billion in AUM with 22% annualized returns over the past year, outperforming the MSCI World Index by 450 basis points. This reflects our active tilts toward high-conviction themes like AI infrastructure and quality growth stocks, enhanced by Apex Insight's dynamic factor models. In Q4, we captured upside from the Magnificent Seven while hedging volatility through low-vol overlays. Client feedback has been strong, with inflows accelerating amid market rallies, and we're positioning for continued earnings-driven gains in 2025.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Apex Asset Management. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
